stem:
A 4-year-old boy presents for a planned health check and immunisations. You have never met him before. His mother reports delayed walking (at 2 years), ongoing unsteady gait, and delayed speech. On examination he is not dysmorphic, has very large calves, a waddling gait, and a Gowers sign. Tone is normal, proximal power is reduced, and reflexes are elicited only with reinforcement. Cranial nerves, coordination, sensation, and cardiovascular examination are normal.

Which of the following blood tests would you expect to be raised?
explanation: The presentation is classic for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a progressive proximal myopathy causing delayed motor milestones, calf pseudohypertrophy, waddling gait, and Gowers sign. Creatine kinase is markedly elevated due to muscle breakdown.
rationale: Selected the best existing option without rewriting because the stem and options already support a single best answer.

optionExplanations.A: Seen in myasthenia gravis, which causes fatigable weakness rather than calf hypertrophy and Gowers sign.
optionExplanations.B: Alpha-fetoprotein is not the expected raised blood test in this presentation.
optionExplanations.C: Calcium is not characteristically elevated in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: creatine kinase is elevated in muscular dystrophy due to muscle fibre damage.

Instructions

Question 3 - 5 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 4 year old boy visits presents to you for his planned health check and immunisations. You have never met him before. You enquire about his developmental history and learn that he walked at 2 years and is still not very stable on his feet. He also didn’t start talking until he was 22 months which his mum says ‘runs in the family’. His mother is not concerned about his hearing or vision. He has an elder sister who is 6 and is thriving in school.

On examination the boy is not dysmorphic. His weight is 15kg (25th centile) and his height is 97cm (25th centile). His head circumference is 48cm (25th centile). When you examine his gait you notice he has very large calves and he walks with a waddling gait. When you get him to rise up from lying on the floor, he turns himself over and then uses his hands to push himself up from the floor. His tone is normal; his power is 4/5 proximally at the hips and shoulders but normal peripherally. You elicit deep tendon reflexes with reinforcement. His cranial nerve exam is normal. His coordination is normal as is his sensory exam. His cardiovascular examination is normal.
